messages:
Ana M: Heads-up — planning to deploy runtime change v1.4.2 tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Requesting deploy owner + rollback gate review. Main change: kernel-selection tweak to improve throughput for long sequences.

Ryan C: I can own the deploy. I'll be on-call at the laptop during the window. What are the specific smoke checks and rollback criteria we want to lock in?

Keiko: I will run smoke checks and watch metrics (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, GPU OOMs, pod restarts). Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-readiness (updated w/ checklist).

Sara L: Quick runbook notes from my review. Proposed rollback criteria (if any met, immediate rollback unless otherwise argued and approved):
- sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m OR 3x baseline error rate
- p95 latency increase > 40% AND p95 > 800ms
- Canary inference outputs diverge from golden set (semantic diff threshold exceeded)
- OOMs / worker crash loops / repeated pod restarts (>3 restarts in 10m)
- Any customer-facing throttles or client-visible failures

Tom B: For detection I'll add a temporary alert for the window: model-serving-error-rate and pod-restart spike. I can create a Grafana alert scoped to the canary namespace.

Ryan C: Rollback plan summary: 1) pause/scale down new variant 2) switch canary traffic back to previous revision (traffic manager) 3) drain/restart affected nodes 4) if changes included infra migrations (none here) revert DB changes 5) notify customers if needed. Script: scripts/rollback.sh <rev> handles 1-2.

Keiko: Smoke check checklist (short, to run after canary deploy):
1) curl /health -> 200 and /metrics present
2) run 3 sample generations against canary and compare to golden outputs
3) embeddings sanity check for 5 sample inputs (consistency)
4) GPU memory per-pod < 80% and no OOM logs
5) KV cache warming observed in logs (cache hit rate rising)

Commands to run locally: 
```bash
for p in "what is redwood?" "summarize this text" "translate hello"; do
  curl -s -X POST https://canary-api.redwood.test/generate \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"prompt\":\"$p\"}" | jq -r .text
done
```

Sara L: Operational gates: if canary not healthy within 10 minutes -> rollback. If we see partial degradation in first 30 minutes but limited to non-critical SLOs, hold and escalate to #incidents; do not continue ramp without explicit approval.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by Ryan C for 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z. Canary traffic: 5% for 10m -> 25% for 20m -> 100% if all green.

Ana M: OK. Owners: Ryan (deploy), Keiko (smoke), Tom (alerting), Sara (go/no-go). Please acknowledge with :thumbsup: if you accept these gates.

Ryan C: :thumbsup:

Keiko: :thumbsup: I'll paste results in this thread and in the runbook doc.

Tom B: ack — I'll add the alert and test it 30m before the window.

Sara L: :thumbsup: I'll be monitoring the dashboards during ramp.

Ryan C: Small note for rollback operator: use `scripts/rollback.sh <previous-rev>` — it flips traffic and performs a health-checked wait. If traffic switch fails, manual traffic-manager override is at /admin/traffic.

Keiko: Added the smoke checklist to the runbook page and pinned the golden-output samples.

deploy-bot: reminder scheduled: 30 minutes until deploy window for v1.4.2.

Ana M: Thanks team — appreciate fast ack. We'll reconvene in this thread for pre-deploy checks and post-canary status updates.
